name: Avail
label: Lookout!
lede: A suburban hardcore band moved from the D.C. suburbs to Richmond in 1990 and never stopped writing about it: the river, the streets, the neighborhoods, the friends it lost.

eras.title: Reston kids, Richmond lifers
eras.text: Avail started in the Northern Virginia suburb of Reston and only became itself after moving to Richmond, where guitarist Joe Banks recruited a singer from a rival band. From then on the city was the subject.

years.p: The founders: guitarist [[Joe Banks|e7e35c4c-475b-4c7e-9671-893312c16ad5]], singer Brien Stewart, drummer Doug Crosby and bassist Mikey Warstler. Banks is the only one still in the band.

years.h: Avail moves to Richmond and takes Tim Barry from a rival band
years.p: Joe Banks relocated the band to Richmond around 1990 and joined forces with [[Tim Barry|300184e2-cb52-478c-9541-a6d0db1b7257]] of the rival group Learning Disabled Kids.
The first of Avail's six studio albums, made soon after the move to Richmond.

eras.title: Lookout! and the Richmond records
eras.text: Signed to Lookout!, the Berkeley label that had just broken Green Day, Avail cut three records that put Richmond streets in the song titles. The stretch ends with Over the James, the album that later made the Decibel Hall of Fame.

years.h: Dixie on Lookout! Records, with a John Mellencamp cover
years.p: Recorded in June 1994 at Uncle Punchy Studios in Silver Spring, Maryland. The twelve originals come with a cover of John Mellencamp's Pink Houses.

years.h: Tim Barry plays bass in (Young) Pioneers
years.p: From 1994 to 1995 Barry doubled as bassist for Richmond folk-punk band [[(Young) Pioneers|642ef2de-0d93-45aa-a27c-a93f32ebfbbb]], who shared a split with Avail.

years.h: 4am Friday is named for the hour a friend died
years.p: Avail titled its third album after the day and time the band heard that Bob Baynor of [[Maximillian Colby|ed0c2410-784d-489e-864e-17c3ebeffd7d]] had died. The song F.C.A. is about him.
years.xp:
Recorded January to February 1996, again at Uncle Punchy in Silver Spring, and released on Lookout! Pitchfork later gave it 8.3.

Simple Song, from the same record, landed on the Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 4 soundtrack in 2002.

years.h: Over the James recorded at Montana Studio in Richmond
years.p: Avail tracked the album at home in Richmond, after two records made in Silver Spring, Maryland.

years.h: Over the James: Richmond's streets become song titles
years.p: Fourteen songs steeped in Avail's city, including Lombardy St. and Scuffle Town. Pitchfork called it the apotheosis of Avail's sound.
years.xp:
Pitchfork's Zach Baron also called it slicker, slower and sorta pretentious, and still gave it 7.7. AllMusic gave three stars.

In May 2019 Decibel inducted it into its Hall of Fame, calling it a melodic hardcore classic that reached both emo and metal fans.

years.h: Live at the Bottom of the Hill in San Francisco
years.p: Lookout! released an Avail live album taped at the San Francisco club Bottom of the Hill.

eras.title: Fat Wreck, then the long quiet
eras.text: Avail moved to Fat Wreck Chords for two more records, both made in Richmond. After Front Porch Stories there were no new albums, Tim Barry went solo and acoustic, and in 2007 the band stopped playing without ever saying it had broken up.

years.h: One Wrench, Avail's first for Fat Wreck Chords
years.p: Recorded in March 2000 at Montana Studio in Richmond with Mark Miley. The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette called Avail undersung working-class heroes.

years.h: Front Porch Stories: Avail's last album so far
years.p: Recorded in June 2002 at Sound of Music Studios in Richmond and released on Fat. No Avail studio album has followed.

years.h: Tim Barry starts a solo folk career
years.p: Barry began playing acoustic sets on his own, which led to Rivanna Junction on Chunksaah in 2006 and a string of records since.

years.h: Jade Tree reissues Dixie, 4am Friday and Over the James
years.p: The reissues added bonus material, including covers of [[Embrace|9d1ad8e3-8740-429a-bdc5-52f96a9c4431]], Billy Joel and Elvis Presley on Over the James.

years.h: Avail stops playing live, without ever breaking up
years.p: Wikipedia notes the band ceased performing in 2007 but never officially disbanded.

eras.title: Back at The National
eras.text: Twelve years after its last show, Avail announced one Richmond date and kept going. Over the James got its Hall of Fame nod and its own anniversary shows.

years.h: Avail's reunion: The National, Richmond, July 19, 2019
years.p: Announced on March 26, 2019: Tim Barry, Joe Banks, Gwomper, Erik Larson and hype man Beau Beau Butler, back in their city.

years.h: Decibel puts Over the James in its Hall of Fame
years.p: The metal magazine inducted Avail's 1998 album as a melodic hardcore classic.

years.h: Avail plays Over the James shows for its 25th year
years.p: Punknews reported the lineup for Avail's Over the James 2023 show in Richmond.
